Integration

A spot field spreading outward from wherever the coat is already dark - merging into solid patches close in, thinning to isolated marks a foot or two out, and gone beyond that.

What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 595 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/integration.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Integration

It does not choose its own places; it grows out of the ones the horse already has. Anywhere the coat is dark - the crest and the base of the mane, a dorsal stripe, the distal limbs, the margin of any other marking - becomes a source, and elements propagate outward from it. Right at a source they merge into continuous patches with scalloped margins; a hand's span out they are separate circles and lobes with their long axis pointing the way they came; further still they thin to nothing. It reads as an appaloosa blanket at medium scale.

  1. elements spreading out of the dark — SPOTS × PIGMENT, painted with TOWARD
  2. the merged patches nearest the source — PIGMENT × PATCHES, painted with TOWARD

Coloured Integration

The same marking in a colour the line carries rather than in white. Fully recessive: it takes two copies, and a single copy beside a white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes, whatever the white form does.

  1. elements spreading out of the dark, in colour — SPOTS × PIGMENT, painted with TOWARD
  2. the merged patches nearest the source, in colour — PIGMENT × PATCHES, painted with TOWARD
